Write $\operatorname{supp}(P):=\{a\in\mathcal A:P(a)>0\}$. For $a^n=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathcal A^n$, its empirical distribution is $\widehat P_{a^n}(a):=n^{-1}|\{t:a_t=a\}|$. For $\delta>0$, define the support-restricted strongly typical set by
$$T_\delta^{(n)}(P):=\{a^n\in\operatorname{supp}(P)^n:|\widehat P_{a^n}(a)-P(a)|\le\delta P(a)\text{ for every }a\text{ with }P(a)>0\}.$$
For a finite joint law $P_{XA}$ and a fixed $x^n$, write $T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{A|X}\mid x^n):=\{a^n:(x^n,a^n)\in T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{XA})\}$. This conditional set is empty if $x^n$ is outside the support of $P_X$. Zero-probability letters are excluded exactly, so no logarithm of zero occurs in likelihood calculations on these sets.

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

derivations.claim: Under the product law $q^{\otimes n}$, every $a^n\in T_q$ has probability $\prod_a q(a)^{n_a}=\exp(-nH(q))$, omitting zero-count coordinates. Since the total probability of $T_q$ is at most one, $|T_q|\exp(-nH(q))\le1$, which gives the upper bound.

To bound the probability of $T_q$ below, compare it with an arbitrary attainable type $r$ with counts $m_a=nr(a)$. If $m_a>0=n_a$ for some $a$, then $\Pr_{q^{\otimes n}}(T_r)=0$. Otherwise let $k_a=m_a-n_a$ for each $a$ with $n_a>0$. The ratio is $\frac{\Pr_{q^{\otimes n}}(T_r)}{\Pr_{q^{\otimes n}}(T_q)}=\frac{\prod_a n_a!}{\prod_a m_a!}\prod_{a:n_a>0}\left(\frac{n_a}{n}\right)^{k_a}.$ For $k_a\ge0$, the corresponding factor is at most $n^{-k_a}$ because $(n_a+1)\cdots(n_a+k_a)\ge n_a^{k_a}$. For $k_a=-s_a<0$, it is at most $n^{s_a}$ because $n_a(n_a-1)\cdots(n_a-s_a+1)\le n_a^{s_a}$. The equal-total-count relation gives $\sum_{k_a>0}k_a=\sum_{k_a<0}s_a$, so the product of these bounds is at most one. Thus $T_q$ has maximum probability among all type classes under $q^{\otimes n}$.

Each of the $m$ counts has at most $n+1$ values, so there are at most $(n+1)^m$ types. Their probabilities sum to one; since $T_q$ is a most probable type class by step 1.2, its probability is at least $(n+1)^{-m}$. Using $\Pr(T_q)=|T_q|\exp(-nH(q))$ proves the lower bound.

By independence of the codewords, the probability that none of $M_n$ words lies in the conditional typical set is $(1-p_n(x^n))^{M_n}\le e^{-M_np_n(x^n)}$. For a fixed $x^n$, let $A=T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{XU}|x^n)$. The event that index $\ell$ is the first successful index depends on codewords before $\ell$ failing and the $\ell$th codeword lying in $A$; those events are independent across codewords. For each attainable joint type of $(U_J,U_{J^c},S)$ compatible with this block, the number of possible $u_J^n$ is a product of conditional type-class sizes, hence at most $\exp(nH_q(U_J|U_{J^c},S))$ by [F2]. There are at most $(n+1)^m$ such types, where $m=|\mathcal S|\prod_i|\mathcal U_i|$. Since finite entropy is continuous on each finite simplex (each summand $-t\ln t$ extends continuously at $t=0$), choose the typicality tolerance small enough that every such type has $H_q(U_J|U_{J^c},S)\le H(U_J|U_{J^c},S)+\eta/3$. Therefore the conditional-typical fan has at most $(n+1)^m\exp(n(H(U_J|U_{J^c},S)+\eta/3))$ candidates.

Every such candidate tuple has marginal types close to the target $P_{U_i}$. For a fixed tuple of codewords, its product-marginal probability is $\prod_{i\in J}P_{U_i}^{\otimes n}(u_i^n)=\exp(n\sum_{i\in J}\sum_{u_i}\widehat P_{u_i^n}(u_i)\ln P_{U_i}(u_i))$, which is at most $\exp[-n(\sum_{i\in J}H(U_i)-\eta/3)]$ when the tolerance is sufficiently small. For any fixed candidate combination, its changed codewords are independent of the source and the codebooks at indices in $J^c$. The indicator of a typical true tuple is bounded by the indicator that its complementary block is typical; this latter block is independent of the changed codewords, so step 2.1 bounds the candidate typicality probability after conditioning on it.
